brief_item.title: GPU并行图聚类加速Louvain与Leiden
brief_item.direction_name: GPU集群、分布式训练与工程可靠性
brief_item.core_conclusion: 论文提出pLouvain和pLeiden，把Louvain、Leiden的局部移动、图收缩与细化改写为GPU并行流程，并用对称破除模拟有序遍历。57个图数据集上，两者相对最快开源并行实现分别获得3.1倍和8.8倍几何平均加速，pLeiden的并行细化保持Leiden质量保证。
brief_item.mechanism: pLouvain用GPU内核并行执行局部移动和图收缩，两个阶段采用同步高并发。pLeiden用基于生成树的并行细化替代顺序细化，并证明可达到原细化可达的聚类结果。
brief_item.result: 两种方法在57个图中的56个上取得高于所有对手的模块度，图收缩子程序几何平均至少快15倍。加入反粗化后运行时间增加29.0%，模块度增加0.0127。
brief_item.boundary: 证据来自NVIDIA B200上的图聚类基准，不等同于AI训练或服务收益。论文未报告多GPU扩展、能耗、内存压力、故障恢复或下游任务质量。
brief_item.project_relevance: 它可作为仓库图、依赖聚类和拓扑调度的GPU原语，但不能直接证明Agent检索或分布式训练变快。接入前应测量图构建成本、更新频率、显存占用和下游搜索质量。

facts.title: GPU-Accelerated Multilevel Graph Clustering: A Parallel Perspective on Louvain and Leiden
facts.event_hint: arXiv:2608.01503v1 introduces GPU-parallel pLouvain and pLeiden multilevel graph clustering
facts.problem: Louvain and Leiden community detection are useful on large graphs, but existing parallel implementations leave substantial GPU performance and quality gaps; Leiden parallelizations also lacked a proof that the sequential algorithm's quality guarantees were preserved.
facts.mechanism: pLouvain parallelizes the Louvain+ local-move and graph-contraction phases with GPU-centric kernels, synchronous high-concurrency execution, and lightweight symmetry breaking that emulates ordered vertex traversal. pLeiden replaces Leiden's sequential refinement with a spanning-tree-based parallel refinement whose reachable clusterings are proven equivalent to the original refinement, thereby preserving Leiden's quality guarantees. Both optimize the LambdaCC objective and share GPU graph-contraction and traversal subroutines.

evidence.claim: Across 57 graphs from 10 families, pLouvain achieved a 3.1× geometric-mean speedup over the fastest open-source parallel Louvain competitor, while pLeiden achieved 8.8× over the fastest open-source parallel Leiden competitor.
evidence.baseline: Current fastest open-source parallelizations of Louvain and Leiden
evidence.condition: 57-graph, 10-family collection; headline results primarily measured on an NVIDIA B200 GPU.

evidence.claim: pLouvain and pLeiden+ produced higher modularity than any competitor on 56 of 57 tested graphs; the best overall method on every graph was either pLouvain or pLeiden+.
evidence.baseline: Compared with the evaluated CPU/GPU Louvain and Leiden implementations
evidence.condition: Modularity comparison on the 57-graph test set; pLeiden without uncoarsening was lower quality on average.

evidence.claim: The graph-contraction implementation was at least 15× faster by geometric mean than state-of-the-art competitors in the paper's contribution summary.
evidence.condition: GPU graph-contraction subroutine; exact per-graph distribution is not stated in the abstract.

evidence.claim: pLeiden's spanning-tree refinement is designed to preserve all six original Leiden quality guarantees, while pLeiden+ adds an uncoarsening phase for quality.
evidence.condition: Theoretical equivalence claim for the parallel refinement; runtime/quality trade-offs remain implementation-dependent.

evidence.claim: In the single-iteration comparison, graph contraction averaged 6.5% of pLouvain runtime and reached at most 12.6% on any graph; adding uncoarsening increased runtime by 29.0% and modularity by 0.0127.
evidence.baseline: pLouvain without the corresponding uncoarsening or contraction variant
evidence.condition: Ablation and component analysis over the tested graph collection.

facts.evaluation_context: The paper evaluates pLouvain, pLeiden, and pLeiden+ against v-Louvain, GVE, Networkit, cuGraph, and GALA implementations on 57 graphs from 10 families. GPU experiments primarily use an NVIDIA B200 with 180 GB VRAM; CPU baselines use an AMD Ryzen 9950X3D. Runtimes are collected across repeated runs and summarized with geometric means, while clustering quality is measured by modularity. The algorithms optimize LambdaCC or modularity-compatible objectives.
facts.limitations: The evidence is a graph-clustering benchmark rather than an end-to-end AI-training or serving workload. Headline speedups are tied to the tested B200 GPU, graph families, implementations, compiler/runtime settings, and objective; they do not establish the same gains on other GPUs, graph distributions, or production pipelines. pLeiden's quality guarantees are theoretical, while pLeiden without uncoarsening can be slower/lower quality than pLouvain and pLeiden+. The paper reports modularity and runtime, not energy, memory pressure, multi-GPU scaling, fault recovery, or downstream task quality.
facts.project_relevance: The work is a useful GPU-parallel primitive for graph-based repository maps, dependency clustering, or topology-aware scheduling, but it is not direct evidence of faster agent context retrieval or distributed-training throughput. Any integration would need to measure graph-construction cost, update frequency, memory footprint, and downstream search quality in the target agent or infrastructure workload.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF was fetched and the title matches the input metadata exactly.
Speedups and quality counts are reported with graph-set and hardware conditions; no cross-hardware generalization is inferred.
